svg.title: How traffic reaches Smarter, and leaves it
svg.desc: Users and clients on the internet resolve each host name in Route53, which has one record per host and no wildcard, and connect to one AWS Network Load Balancer in the VPC's public subnets, on ports 80 and 443 only. The load balancer passes the TCP connection, with the proxy protocol, to Traefik in the private subnets, which terminates TLS with a cert-manager certificate from Let's Encrypt, redirects HTTP to HTTPS, sets HSTS and CORS, and forwards plain HTTP to the smarter-api pods on port 8000. Calico, on every node, enforces the platform namespace's network policies: default deny, so only the platform's pods reach MariaDB and Redis. The pods leave the VPC through a NAT gateway, to LLM providers, APIs and AWS's public endpoints, and reach S3 through a gateway endpoint that keeps that traffic inside AWS.
svg.text: How traffic reaches Smarter, and leaves it
one load balancer in, one NAT gateway out; TLS ends at Traefik; Calico polices the traffic between pods
the nodes, and the cluster's API: no public IP
